result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend ranking by expected loss plus a capped hold tier, reject option A, and present the setting as outcome counts the AP manager can adjust. Answer A wins on item 2 because it says outright that paying can't easily be undone while a hold can be released; Answer B mostly treats holds as costly and never names reversibility. Answer B is better on checking misses, with a post-payment sample audit, a calibration step and a tracked metric for duplicates found after payment. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend ranking by expected loss plus a small capped hold tier, and both turn the threshold into per-day counts the manager can see. B states plainly that paying is hard to undo while a hold can be released. It also covers more of what happens below the line (due-date surfacing, a dry-run rollout) and how to see misses (a skipped list shown closest-to-flagged first, and no unmeasured accuracy figures). A mostly treats holds as costly and never contrasts a hold with paying or rejecting, though its post-payment sample audit and calibration advice are strong.
